          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned in IA No. 283229/2026 and IA No. 283231/2026.
2. Issue notice to respondent Nos. 1 to 23, returnable on
28.10.2026.
1

--- Page 258 ---
3. Ms. Kanti, learned AOR accepts notice on behalf of respondent
Nos.2, 3, 4, 8, 10, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22.  Ms. Srishti Mishra,
learned AOR accepts notice on behalf of respondent Nos.5, 6, 7, 15,
16 and 17.  
4. Respondent No.1 may be served through standing counsel also.
5. Liberty is granted to the petitioner as well as to the private
respondents to place on record translated copies of the statements
of the relevant witnesses, and of any other material documents on
which they may seek to rely.
I.A. No. 285335/2026  
6. This application for intervention has been preferred by Mr.
Maniar Kalpesh Kumar, seeking, inter alia, the following reliefs: 
a)  allow  the  present  Application  and  permit  the
Applicant to intervene in and be impleaded as a party
respondent in Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary
No. 48619 of 2026;
b) permit the Applicant to file written submissions and
to be heard, in person or through counsel, at the
hearing of the captioned Special Leave Petition and of
any appeal arising therefrom;
c) be pleased to expunge the observations and findings
recorded against the Applicant in paragraph 43 of the
common final judgment and order dated 07.05.2026 passed
by the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay in
Criminal Appeal No. 641 of 2019 with Criminal Appeal
No.  656  of  2019,  insofar  as  the  same  attribute
suppression of material, oblique motive and political
instigation to the Applicant;
d) be pleased to grant leave to the Applicant to assail
the order dated 30.12.2014 passed by the Ld. Special
Judge (CBI), City Civil and Sessions Court, Greater
Mumbai  in  Discharge  Application  (Exhibit  232)  in
Sessions Case Nos. 177 of 2013, 178 of 2013, 577 of
2013 and 312 of 2014; and
e) pass such other and further orders as this Hon'ble
2

--- Page 259 ---
Court  may  deem  fit  and  proper  in  the  facts  and
circumstances of the case.
7. It appears that the Applicant had preferred Interim
Application No. 1172 of 2026 in Criminal Appeal No. 641 of
2019 before the High Court, seeking leave to be impleaded as
a party to the said appeal and assailing the order dated
30.12.2014 passed by the learned Special Judge (CBI), whereby
Accused No. 16, namely, Amit Anilchandra Shah, came to be
discharged.
8.  The  High  Court,  vide the  impugned  judgment  dated
07.05.2026,  dismissed  the  said  Interim  Application  for
reasons which may be briefly noticed. It was found that the
Applicant had suppressed the fact that Criminal Application
No. 1248 of 2015, preferred by one Mr. Harsh Mander on
similar grounds, had been dismissed by the learned Special
Judge (CBI) on 11.03.2016, and that the challenge thereto in
SLP (Crl.) No. 5000 of 2016 had also been turned down by this
Court on 01.08.2016. The High Court further observed that the
Applicant had offered no explanation as to: (i) how he came
to learn that the High Court had reserved judgment; (ii) his
locus qua the pending appeals; and (iii) why he sought to
assail the proceedings arising out of Crime No. 5 of 2005
more  than  two  decades  after  its  registration.  These
circumstances, in the view of the High Court, cast doubt on
the bona fides of the Applicant.
3

--- Page 260 ---
9. We find no reason to differ from the view taken by the
High Court, or to interfere with it. This is all the more so
because the Applicant, even in the application filed before
this Court, has nowhere disclosed: (i) what locus he has in
the matter; (ii) on what basis this Court ought to implead
him; and (iii) how his submissions bear any relevance to the
present criminal proceedings. Furthermore, the Applicant has
not satisfied us as to why this Court should reopen the order
dated 30.12.2014 passed by the learned Special Judge (CBI),
which has since attained finality, having never been assailed
either  by  the  Respondent-CBI  or  by  the  family  of  the
deceased-victims.
10. It is trite law that a third-party intervenor, such as
the Applicant herein, has no locus standi to intervene in
criminal proceedings, and that a stranger to the proceedings
can have no role in a prosecution instituted by the State. 
11. Further, this Court had already been seized of the
matter, and a similar prayer made in SLP (Crl.) No. 5000 of
2016 stood rejected in limine.
12. We, therefore, are unable to discern as to why the same
issue is now sought to be re-agitated, or why this Court
should return a finding contrary to what has already been
settled by the learned Special Judge (CBI), the High Court
and, earlier, by this Court itself. We are, thus, of the
considered  view  that  the  present  application  is  a
misconceived attempt on the part of the Applicant to impede
4

--- Page 261 ---
the proceedings and to reopen issues which have long since
attained finality.
13. In this light, we are satisfied that the High Court has
assigned cogent reasons, and we are not inclined to interfere
with the findings recorded in paragraph 43 of the impugned
judgment dated 07.05.2026. Accordingly, I.A. No. 285335/2026
stands dismissed. 
14. Ordered accordingly.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)

1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. Appellant is an accused in Crime No.371 of 2025
registered at Majholi Police Station in the District of
Sidhi (Madhya Pradesh) under Sections 8/20(B) of the
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
(briefly the ‘NDPS Act’ hereinafter).
4. Allegation against the appellant is that on search of
the vehicle in which appellant was travelling, two gunny
bags were recovered; one containing 25.700 kgs. Of ganja
and the other bag containing 22.600 kgs of ganja. Thus a
total of 48.300 kgs of ganja was recovered from the joint
possession of the appellant and the other co-accused.
5. Appellant is in custody since 04.04.2025.
6. The High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur (briefly
1

--- Page 267 ---
the ‘High Court’ hereinafter)  vide  the impugned order
dated 16.04.2026 declined to grant bail to the appellant.
7. This Court had issued notice on 10.08.2026, pursuant
to which State has filed counter affidavit. In the
counter affidavit, it is pointed out that petitioner has
got a total of 11 criminal antecedents, out of which 3
are NDPS cases. Insofar trial is concerned, charge sheet
was submitted whereafter charges have been framed and
trial has commenced. Out of 16 prosecution witnesses, 4
have been examined.
8. When this was brought to the notice of learned
counsel for the appellant and when the Court asked him
whether he would like to file rejoinder affidavit to
explain the antecedents, he submitted that he is ready
with the case as all materials have been disclosed in the
Special Leave Petition. According to him, there is no
need to file rejoinder affidavit.
9. In the synopsis, we find that appellant has indeed
mentioned about all the criminal antecedents including
the 3 NDPS cases but his comment in all the three cases
are verbatim the same i.e., false cases are registered
against him because of the appellant residing in the
vicinity of the Police Station.
10. Even if we discard the other cases which are pending
against him which may be of relatively minor offences, in
the face of 3 pending NDPS cases against the appellant,
we are not inclined to grant bail to the appellant at
2

--- Page 268 ---
this stage.
11. Accordingly the criminal appeal is dismissed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

had mercilessly beaten her in a room with iron rods and

1

--- Page 271 ---

recorded the following:
1. In the hearing today, learned counsel for
the respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh has
informed  us  that  out  of  14  witnesses,

7. In  the  hearing  today,  learned  counsel  for  the

sixth prosecution witnesses is presently going on. Next
date of hearing before the Trial Court is today.
8. In our order dated 27.07.2026, we had requested the
Trial Court to grant shorter dates for examination of the
witnesses. Till 27.07.2026, five witnesses were examined.
Two months have passed by since then. Examination of only
the sixth witness is going on.

been informed at the Bar that appellant is now above 70
2

--- Page 272 ---
years of age. Though the allegation, on the face of it,
appears serious, nonetheless we will have to balance the
interest of the prosecution and the accused. Appellant is
in custody as an under-trial for more than 4 years now
with no end to the criminal trial on sight. In such
circumstances, we are of the view appellant should be
enlarged on bail.
10. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order of the
High Court dated 08.09.2025 and direct that the appellant
shall be produced before the Trial Court within a maximum
period of 7 days from today whereafter he shall be
enlarged on bail on such terms and conditions as may be

1. Leave granted.

1

--- Page 275 ---
6. On 27.07.2026, this Court had issued notice and

the appellant cooperating with the investigation.
7. In the hearing today, learned Additional Advocate
General  Mr.  D.S.  Parmar,  has  fairly  submitted  that

ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Uttar Pradesh.
3. Appellant(s) is aggrieved by order dated 10.04.2026
passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the
regular bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in Case Crime No.87/2025
registered at Police Station- Nehtaur, District- Bijnor,
Uttar Pradesh under Sections 80(2) and 85 of the Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’) read with Sections
3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
5. Appellant  is  the  mother-in-law  of  the  deceased.
Deceased had died under unnatural circumstances in her
matrimonial home within 06 months of marriage.
1

--- Page 291 ---
6. Appellant was arrested on 13.05.2025 and has been in
custody since then.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
03.08.2026, pursuant to which learned counsel for the
respondent-State  of  Uttar  Pradesh  has  filed  counter
affidavit.
8. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
appellant is a 62 years old lady and has already suffered
incarceration for almost one and half years. Trial is
proceeding at a snail’s pace and it will be a while before
the  trial  can  be  concluded.  In  such  circumstances,
appellant may be enlarged on bail.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent-State of Uttar
Pradesh submits that as of now, 02 witnesses have been
examined out of the total of 16 materials witnesses.
10. On a query by the Court, he fairly submits that there
is no direct role attributed to the appellant.
11. Without expressing any opinion at this stage but
balancing the interest of the prosecution as well as that
of the accused, we are of the view that it would be just
and proper if the accused is enlarged on bail.
12. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
10.04.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
13. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the concerned Sessions Court within a
maximum period of 07 days from today, whereafter she shall
be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
2

--- Page 292 ---
deemed appropriate. Needless to say, appellant shall co-
operate  with  the  trial  and  not  seek  unnecessary

UMESH YADAV      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
THE STATE OF BIHAR     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Bihar.
3. Appellant(s) is aggrieved by order dated 23.02.2026
passed by the High Court of Judicature at Patna (briefly
the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the regular bail
application of the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in FIR No.37/2025 registered
at Police Station- Bahera, District- Gaya, Bihar under
Sections 8/17(c) and 18(c) of the Narcotics Drugs and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short, ‘NDPS Act’).
5. The allegation against the appellant is that he is
the owner and driver of the truck in question which was
coming from Jharkhand. Acting on confidential information,
the truck was intercepted and upon search, 03 bags of
poppy straw were recovered and seized. Each bag contained
1

--- Page 295 ---
more than 21 kgs of poppy straw.
6. Appellant was arrested on 18.03.2025 and since then,
he has been in custody.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
20.08.2026, pursuant to which the respondent-State of
Bihar has filed counter affidavit.
8. After narrating the facts leading to the arrest of
the  appellant,  it  is  stated  that  on  completion  of
investigation, charge-sheet dated 11.06.2025 was filed
against the appellant under Sections 8/17(c) and 18(c) of
the NDPS Act. As per the charge-sheet, there are total 04
prosecution witnesses who are proposed to be examined.
Subsequently,  charges  have  been  framed  against  the
appellant. Trial Court has fixed 01.10.2026 as the next
date of the trial.
9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
going through the materials on record, we are of the view
that appellant has remained in custody for more than one
and half years as of now. The trial has yet not commenced.
Though  the  prosecution  proposes  to  examine  only  04
witnesses, it does not appear that the trial can be
concluded at an early date. That apart, we find that
insofar  poppy  straw  is  concerned,  the  threshold  for
commercial quantity is 50 kgs. In the circumstances, we
are of the view that appellant may be enlarged on bail.
10. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
23.02.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
2

--- Page 296 ---
11. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the jurisdictional Special Court within a
maximum period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall
be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
deemed appropriate.
12. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

1. The application for exemption from filing certificate of
a Senior Advocate is rejected as under Order XLVIII, Rule 2(2) of
the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, it is mandatory for any Curative
Petition to be accompanied by a certificate from a Senior Advocate.
2. The application for permission to appear and argue in
person is also rejected.
3. The Curative Petition is defective for the reasons stated
in  the  Office  Report.  The  defects  were  communicated  to  the
petitioner-in-person but he has not cured the same so far.
4. However, instead of rejecting this petition for non-
prosecution, we have gone through the same on merits.

--- Page 319 ---
2
5. In  our  opinion,  no  case  to  entertain  the  Curative
Petition is made out within the parameters indicated by this Court
in the case of Rupa Ashok Hurra  vs. Ashok Hurra & Anr. , (2002) 4
SCC 388.
6. Hence, the Curative Petition is dismissed.
7. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications, if
any, also stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.             OF 2026
[ARISING OUT OF SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRL.)
NO.11047/2026]
VICKY SHARMA                                  Appellant(s)
                           VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA & ANR.                       Respondent(s)
O R D E R
 1. Leave granted.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. This appeal arises from an order dated 18.03.2025
passed  by  the  High  Court  of  Punjab  and  Haryana  at
Chandigarh rejecting the anticipatory bail prayer of the
appellant in connection with First Information Report
(FIR) No.512 of 17.09.2024 registered at Police Station
City Tohana, District Fatehabad, Chandigarh.
4. After considering the submissions on behalf of the
appellant on 02.06.2026, an interim protection order was
passed whereunder the appellant was required to deposit
Rs.12 Lakhs in the Registry of this Court.
5. As  per  the  office  report  dated  26.09.2026,  the
appellant has deposited the amount of Rs.12 lakhs in the
1

--- Page 327 ---
Registry.
6. From the submissions of the learned counsel for the
parties, it appears that the persons who were taken to
Belarus  instead  of  Russia  have  returned  back  and,
therefore, a custodial interrogation may not be required.
In such circumstances, we deem it appropriate to affirm
the  interim  relief  granted  earlier  subject  to  the
following three conditions:
(i) The  appellant  shall  co-operate  in  the
investigation  and  make  himself  available  for
interrogation as and when required by the investigating
agency;
(ii) Within three weeks from today, he shall submit
bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court
concerned along with an undertaking that he shall not
threaten the witnesses or tamper the evidence and;
(iii)  The  amount  of  Rs.12  lakhs  deposited  in  the
Registry of this Court shall be transmitted to the
Court of Session, Fatehabad (State of Haryana).
7. The said deposit shall abide by the result of the
Trial.  In case the police submits a final report (closure
report) or the appellant is discharged in the proceedings,
it shall be open for the appellant to apply for release of
the amount.  It is also clarified that t he amount so
2

--- Page 328 ---
remitted shall be invested in an interest bearing Fixed
Term Deposit of a Nationalised Bank initially for period
of six months which shall be renewed every six months.
8. The appeal is disposed of in the above terms.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
SLP(C)  Nos. 34078-34093/2026:
1. We have heard learned senior counsel for the respective
parties.
2. Learned senior counsel for the respondents at the
outset  drew  our  attention  to  the  fact  that  on
31.07.2026 itself the appeals were admitted by the High
Court and an order of status quo qua the land and/or
plots in question was issued till final disposal of the
said appeals. He, therefore, submitted that the said
fact ought to have been brought to the notice of this
Court in SLP (C) No.29252/2026 when this Court issued
notice to the respondents and granted an interim stay
of the impugned order dated 13.07.2026 until further
orders. That it is the very same impugned order which
is assailed in this case also. He, therefore submitted
that since the appeals have been admitted by the High
Court and an interim order has been granted, this Court
may not interfere at this stage. Learned senior counsel
also pointed out that even in these Special Leave
petitions the order dated 31.07.2026 has not been
annexed or pointed out.

--- Page 348 ---
3
3. Learned  senior  counsel  for  the  petitioner(s)  in
response to this submission however stated that since
notice has been issued and an interim order of stay has
been granted by this Court in SLP (C) No.29252/2026 a
similar order may be made in this case also.
4. We have noted that the submissions made at the bar.
Having regard to the subsequent order of the High Court
dated 31.07.2026 as compared to the order impugned
dated 13.07.2026, we find that the High Court has
decided to hear the appeals on merits. Therefore, we do
not find any reason to interfere with the impugned
order. The Special leave Petitions are hence dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
SLP(C)  No.29252/2026
1. Learned counsel, Mr. Sahil Raveen appearing in the
above Special Leave Petition(s) is also an Advocate-on-
Record who has filed SLP(C) No.29252/2026 wherein we
had  issued  notice  and  granted  interim  order  on
22.08.2026. Since this Special Leave Petition also
arises out of the impugned order dated 13.07.2026
impugned in the aforesaid Special leave Petition(s),
which we have dismissed, we direct that this Special
Leave Petition is also taken on board and the same is
also dismissed. 

--- Page 349 ---
4
2. We do so for the sake of consistency and to avoid
contradictory orders passed as against the very same
impugned order of the High Court. 
3. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Pankaj Sharma, Adv.
                   Mr. Pankaj Kumar Singh, Adv.

                   Mr. Raj Singh Rana, AOR
                   Mr. V.s.dubey, Adv.                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Though the cause shown for the delay does not inspire confidence of this
Court, in the interest of justice, delay stands condoned.
2. Petitioner was initially appointed to the post of Gauge Reader (class IV) in the
Work Charge, and he was later assigned the duties of a Data Processor. After 10
years of service, the petitioner made a representation to the respondent(s)-
authorities to consider his case for grant of pay scale of the Data Processor.
When no action was taken, Writ Application No.30602 of 2016 was filed, which
1

--- Page 373 ---
came to be disposed of directing the respondent(s)-authorities to decide the
petitioner’s claim for pay scale of Data Processor in accordance with law and
within a period of three (3) months.
3. On his claim being rejected again on 09.09.2016, he filed second writ petition
in Writ Application No. 61453 of 2016, which came to be disposed of on
07.05.2019 with a liberty to petitioner to independently agitate his claim for
regular pay scale of a Data Processor under the principle of ‘Equal Pay for Equal
Work’. Writ appeal filed challenging the same, also came to be dismissed on
02.07.2019. On claim of the petitioner being rejected again, third writ petition in
Writ Application No.17212 of 2019 came to be filed, which was disposed of
holding that Director had failed to evaluate the core constitutional framework of
‘Equal Pay for Equal Work’ vide order dated 09.01.2024. Hence, the Director
was directed to explicitly issue a fresh independent evaluated speaking order.
4. On such order dated 09.01.2024 being passed, rejecting his claim, petitioner
filed fourth Writ Application No.12246 of 2024 seeking ‘Equal Pay for Equal
Work’.  The said writ petition is now pending before the High Court, and the
matter has been adjourned. The only grievance of the petitioner is that the High
Court may be directed to dispose of the writ petition in a time bound manner.
5. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for petitioner, and after noticing
that earlier writ petitions seems to have been dismissed on merits on the
ground that petitioner is at liberty to seek for appropriate relief and the issue
relating to claim of ‘Equal Pay for Equal Work’ now pending before the High
Court, we would only request the High Court to expeditiously dispose of the writ
petition, subject to cooperation extended by the learned advocates appearing
for the parties.
6. Accordingly the Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(RASHI GUPTA)                                   (AVGV RAMU)

allow the present appeal and set aside the impugned order.

sale transaction. However, as the same has not fructified but
the appellant, Kuldeep Singh, has been retaining the said
amount, we deemed it appropriate to direct refund thereof
along with interest at a suitable rate.

appearing for the appellant fairly states that the sum of
12026 INSC 451

repaid to the respondents with simple interest @ 8% thereon.

annum from the date of the agreement, viz., 04.01.2006, shall

For Respondent(s)  
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioners have been convicted by the
Trial Court for committing offences under Section 302
read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860. The
subject incident occurred on 23.08.1983. Memo of
parties before the Trial Court records that at least
1

--- Page 430 ---
on the date of judgment, the petitioner no. 1 Achhoo
@ Kalloo was aged about 18 years (but appearing to be
about 25 years); petitioner no. 2 Dinesh @ Munna was
aged about 16 years; and petitioner no. 3 Babu Tiwari
was aged about 14 years (but appearing to be about 16
years). Despite such reference to their age, neither
the petitioners claimed to be juvenile on the date of
occurrence, nor the Trial Court or the High Court has
ever made an inquiry as to their juvenility.
2. The petitioners have moved IA No.177056 of
2026 before this Court, claiming that they were
juvenile as on the date of occurrence, therefore an
inquiry  should  be  conducted  to  determine  their
correct age as on the date of occurrence.
3. In view of the above, we direct the concerned
Juvenile Justice Board of the concerned district to
make an inquiry in terms of Section 94 of the
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)
Act, 2015, to determine the age of the petitioners as
on the date of occurrence. For such inquiry, the
Trial Court shall remit a copy of the entire record
of the Trial Court to the Juvenile Justice Board /
concerned competent authority, who will make inquiry
to determine the age of the petitioners as on the
date of occurrence.
4. Needless to say, in course of such inquiry,
both the parties shall be allowed to produce evidence
2

--- Page 431 ---
both oral and documentary. The informant / victims'
family shall also be given an opportunity.
5. List the matter on 18.01.2027 for submission
of report. 
(MINI)                                      (ANU BHALLA)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard learned senior counsel for the parties at a
considerable length.  The relevant records have also been perused
with their able assistance.
2. In sum and substance, it seems to us that the directions to
conduct a forensic audit are primarily directed with respect to the
transactions between FHL, FHHPL and the judgment debtors.  The
directions issued by the High Court in paragraph 274 of the
impugned judgment regarding the forensic audit  qua 17 banks,
therefore, ought to be read and construed in that context.  In
other  words,  these  directions  pertain  to  the  commercial
2

--- Page 440 ---
transactions/ relationships between the judgment debtors, FHL,
FHHPL and the banks.  Clauses x and xi of Paragraph 274 of the
impugned judgment need not be misconstrued as if there is a
direction for a fishing and roving enquiry into the entire affairs
of the banks other than their transactions with FHL, FHHPL and the
judgment debtors.
3. With this clarification, these Special Leave Petitions stand
disposed of, with pending application(s), if any.

facts, this Court does not find any ground or reason to
interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

1.  This Court has passed an order dated 12.05.2026 in
Civil Appeal No.8363 of 2026 (@ SLP (Civil) No.4717 of
2026), “The  New  India  Assurance  Company  Ltd.  Versus  Liya
and  Others”  and the amount of compensation which was
MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION NO.  2636/2026 IN C.A. NO. 8363/2026

--- Page 448 ---
2
awarded by the High Court is Rs.1,27,52,500/- was reduced
to Rs.73,49,500/- by this Court. This Court in paragraph 9
of the order dated 12.05.2026 passed by this Court has
categorically observed that the compensation shall carry
rate of interest at the rate of 8% per annum, as ordered by
the High Court. In considered opinion of this Court, the
aforesaid sentence is in reference to the rate of interest
and nothing more.
2.  The matter was referred to Registrar of this Court
to resolve the dispute and the Registrar in respect of
apportionment has held that the 1st Claimant/Respondent No.1
shall be entitled to 75%, 2nd Claimant/Respondent No.2 shall
be entitled to 12.5% and 3 rd Claimant/Respondent No.3 shall
be entitled to 12.5% of the total amount.
3. In the present case, after the award was passed, the
claimants received a sum of Rs.38,55,344/- along with
interest @ 8% per annum, and the amount arrived at by this
Court was Rs.73,49,500/-. The interest rate applicable, as
per the order of this Court, is 8% per annum, which is the
interest rate awarded by the High Court. In the present
case, the interest payable from 14.01.2015, i.e., the date
of filing of the petition before the MACT, till the date of
actual realization, which is taken to be 23.09.2025 for the
purpose  of  calculation,  comes  to  Rs.32,68,109/-,  and
therefore,  the  total  amount  now  payable  comes  to
Rs.67,62,265/-.
MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION NO.  2636/2026 IN C.A. NO. 8363/2026

--- Page 449 ---
3
4.  This Court is in the considered opinion that the
claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.67,62,265/-. The
remaining amount be credited to the New India Assurance
Company Ltd.-Insurance Company positively within one week
from today.
5.  In view of aforesaid, the Miscellaneous Application
stands disposed of.

RAJNI KUMARI & ORS.        …PETITIONER(S)
VERSUS
AYODHEYA PRASAD & ANR.                     …RESPONDENT(S) 
O R D E R
This is a petition filed under Section 406 of the Code
of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short “Cr.P.C.”). The
petitioner is the wife of the respondent. The petitioner
has filed this Transfer Petition seeking the following
reliefs:
“(a) Transfer the Case being Complaint CT
No.28859 of 2019 titled as “Ayodheya Prasad
Vs. Rajni Kumari & Ors.” pending before the
Court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate First Class-
1, South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi to
the  Court  of  Chief  Judicial  Magistrate,
Patna, Bihar;
(b) pass such other or further orders as
this Hon’ble Court may deem fit and proper in
the interest of justice.”
2. On perusal of the Office Report dated 23.09.2026, it
is noted that the respondent No.1 was served with notice
on 12.08.2026. However, there is no representation on
behalf of respondent No.1. In the circumstances, we have
heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned
Additional Solicitor General appearing for the second
respondent-State.
1

--- Page 514 ---
3. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and
on perusal of the material on record, we find that the
petitioner has made out a case for transfer of the
aforesaid petition.
4. In the result, the Transfer Petition is allowed and
Case  being  Complaint  CT  No.28859  of  2019  titled  as
“Ayodheya Prasad Vs. Rajni Kumari & Ors .” pending before
the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class-1, South
District,  Saket  Courts,  New  Delhi  is  ordered  to  be
transferred to the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Patna, Bihar.
5. Registry to communicate this order to the transferor
Court as well as the transferee Court for taking steps in
accordance with this order. 
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner  before this  Court has  filed the
present petition, being aggrieved by the impugned order
dated 29.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 22321 of
2025, rejecting the second bail application preferred by
the petitioner.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner has straightaway

--- Page 903 ---
argued before this Court that two of the four accused
persons have already been enlarged on bail. It is submitted
that, keeping in view the principles of parity and the fact
that the petitioner has undergone incarceration for a
period of one year and eleven months, the petitioner is
also entitled to be released on bail.
3. On  the  other  hand,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State has drawn the attention of this Court to
the  contents  of  the  FIR  and  read  out  the  specific
allegations levelled against the petitioner. It is pointed
out that a distinct and specific role is attributed to the
petitioner, who assaulted the deceased.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and
upon perusal of the record, this Court is of the opinion
that, given the specific role attributed to the petitioner
and the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, no
case for grant of bail is made out.
5. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  is
dismissed.
6. However, the Trial Court is requested to conclude
the trial as expeditiously as possible at an early date.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

4. The prayer in this petition is for grant of bail in FIR
1

--- Page 955 ---
No.73/2025 dated 13.04.2023, registered at Police Station
Devendra Nagar, Raipur, under Section 4(a) of the Public
Gambling Act, 1867, and under Section 7 of the Chhattisgarh
Gambling (Prohibition) Act, 2022. 
5. The allegations are that the main accused was placing
bets on cricket matches online through Rajshree Online Book.
Based on this information, multiple raids were conducted, and
several people were arrested. The petitioners were arrested on
23.10.2025 and 29.10.2025. A supplementary charge-sheet has
already  been  filed  against  them  after  completion  of
investigation. It is not in dispute that almost 20 co-accused
of the petitioners have already been released on bail.
6. Since the conclusion of trial will take some time and
there is no necessity to keep the petitioners in judicial
custody,  however,  without  expressing  any  opinion  on  the
merits, the prayer for bail is allowed. The petitioners are
directed to be released on bail subject to their furnishing
bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.

grounds raised on behalf of the petitioner, is of the
opinion that the prayer for suspension of sentence deserves
to be allowed. Accordingly, the prayer is allowed.

1. Delay condoned.
2. The submission on behalf of the petitioner(s) is
that they are an autonomous body governed by Mangaluru
Electricity Supply Company Recruitment Regulations, 2002
as per which the minimum qualification prescribed for the
1

--- Page 1017 ---
post of Junior Assistant is “should have PUC qualification
or passed equivalent Examination or Diploma in Accountancy
and Auditing or in Accountancy and costing awarded by the
State  Council  of  Vocational  Education,  Government  of
Karnataka.”
3. It  is  the  submission  of  the  petitioner(s)  that
admittedly the respondent does not have PUC qualification
which is 10 + 2.  Respondent possesses SSLC certificate
and Diploma in automobile. In such circumstances, since
Diploma in Automobile is distinguishable from Diploma in
Accountancy and Auditing, the same could not be considered
equivalent. Besides, the Government circular making the
same as equivalent is not applicable to the petitioner-
organization in light of their own regulations.
4. Issue notice, returnable in six weeks.
5. In the meantime, the effect and operation of the
impugned order shall remain stayed.
